newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile, Mercosur vehicle makers to discuss tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Chile, Mercosur vehicle makers to discuss tariffs.

text.p: Vehicle makers from the four-member Mercosur trade bloc will hold a meeting with their Chilean counterparts in Santiago Tuesday to finalize plans for cutting tariffs in the industry, said a Chilean business group.

If the talks are successful, the companies will present their proposals at government level and tariffs could be cut by the end of the year, said Hugo Baierlein, head of foreign trade at the Sociedad de Fomento Fabril (Sofofa) which represents most of Chilean private industry.
"What is being proposed is lowering all reciprocal (tariffs) to zero," Baierlein told reporters.
"The idea is to reach an agreement in Tuesday's meeting and suggest it (to governments) so that it could come into force in the first months of next year or at the end of this."
"If private companies are in agreement, then governments cannot say no," said Pedro Lizana, president of Sofofa, adding that the talks have gone on for the last 18 months,
The Mercosur trade bloc links Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. Chile has been an associate member since 1996, while Bolivia became the group's second associate this year.
The talks will be held between Sofofa, Chilean vehicle makers and vehicle manufacturing groups Adefa from Argentina and Anfavea from Brazil.
Chile imported vehicles and parts worth $200 million from the Mercosur, while exports to the group -- mainly trucks and buses -- totalled less than $20 million.

Chilean manufacturers' main objective is to persuade the Mercosur to ease its rules of origin which require 60 percent of a vehicle's components to be manufactured within the bloc to benefit from lower tariffs.
Chile, however, has signed trade agreements with Mexico, Venezuela and Bolivia with a limit of 40 percent.
"For us it is very important that Mercosur give us a more flexible rule of origin for a certain time," said Baierlein.
An agreement could open the way to exports to the Mercosur of vehicles assembled in Chile, especially Peugeot vehicles, buses and spare parts.
"At the same time, we are prepared to give unrestricted access so that all cars, pick-ups, trucks and buses can enter (Chile) with a zero tariff," said Baierlein.
Chile's own car industry is small with most vehicles from Asia, Mexico and Brazil. ((-- Rodrigo Martinez, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 x212))
